attempts.summary: Configured VRRP-based dual gateway on node1/node2 so node3 has one stable gateway IP (10.50.13.1) for reaching node4, that stays available with node1 (priority 200) preempting as preferred master and node2 (priority 100) taking over automatically as backup. Discovered topology via ARP capture (node1/node2 eth1 <-> node3, eth2 <-> node4), configured VRRP groups NET-A (vrid 13, VIP 10.50.13.1) and NET-B (vrid 14, VIP 10.50.14.1) on both routers, statically addressed node3/node4's private NICs and added specific routes to each other's subnet via the VRRP VIP. Verified baseline connectivity, disrupted node1 (disabled its private interfaces) and confirmed node2 auto-promoted to MASTER with continuous ping (only ~4s loss during transition), then restored node1 and confirmed it reclaimed MASTER via VRRP preemption. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on all four nodes sequentially (node2, then node1, then node3, then node4), confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of VRRP state, interface config, static routes, and end-to-end connectivity at each step.
